'HINDI PO 'YUNG BUILDING NA 'YON'  

Pinabulaanan ni Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Sec. Vince Dizon na nag-opisina sa nasunog na tanggapan ng ahensya sa Quezon City ang dating asawa ni Brice Hernandez na si Engr. Mel Clarisse Sto. Domingo.  

Muli ring paglilinaw ng kalihim, walang nadamay na mga dokumento at walang pang pinal na report ang Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) hinggil sa pinagmulan ng sunog. Pero base sa paunang imbestigasyon, faulty wiring sa kisame ang dahilan ng insidente.  

Full interview sa comments section.

data.text:
Invest in the Filipino? Clean House First.

As a Filipino who believes in the brilliance and resilience of our people, I welcome any call to invest in the Filipino. But let us be honest: foreign investors do not invest in slogans—they invest in systems.

Despite the President’s appeal at the APEC Summit, the Philippines remains one of the least attractive destinations for foreign investment in Asia. Why?

• Massive corruption continues to plague our institutions, eroding trust and transparency.

• Poor infrastructure hampers mobility, logistics, and competitiveness.

• Unsound economic policies, marked by erratic priorities and short-sighted foreign relations, discourage long-term partnerships.

• Higher taxes burden businesses without delivering commensurate public services.

• Widespread flooding and climate vulnerability threaten stability and safety.

• And most critically, the refusal to engage in bilateral diplomacy in the West Philippine Sea, choosing conflict over cooperation, isolates us even from ASEAN allies who have issued strong statements of concern.

The Filipino people are ready. But the government must first prove that it is.

Before asking the world to invest in us, we must invest in ourselves—by cleaning up corruption, strengthening institutions, and restoring credibility through principled leadership and sound governance.

Only then can we truly say: Invest in the Filipino.

—Dr. Tony Leachon
